chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gives charity and then returns to it (takes it back a portion of it). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'The example of the one who gives charity and then returns to it is like the one who vomits and then returns to his vomit.'

key_terms.يَعُودُ فِي صَدَقَتِهِ: returns to his charity (takes back a portion)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking back part of a charity gift in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the specific ruling of 'returning to charity' (al-'awdah) by citing the Prophet’s metaphor of vomiting and re-consuming one's own vomit. This imagery underscores the spiritual repulsiveness and invalidity of retracting a gift, emphasizing that charity should be given with sincerity and finality rather than as a conditional transaction. The comparison highlights the degradation of the donor’s status when they treat their charitable act as a reversible possession.
